summary: The note explains the science and craft of baking in wood-fired ovens, covering heat transfer by conduction, convection and radiation, the chemistry of oven spring and browning reactions, wood selection, flame management and dough preparation. It cites chefs, bakers and experts and describes 2023 events that renewed interest in the method. It closes with the future of the practice, including the Eco-Flame oven that uses up to 50% less wood.
one_line: An overview of how wood-fired ovens work, the chemistry behind their results, techniques for fire and dough, and the future of the method.
key_facts: Wood-fired ovens cook through conduction, convection, and radiation, unlike gas or electric ovens that heat by surrounding food with hot air.
Wood-fired ovens are traditionally built with brick or stone for their thermal mass, which absorbs heat and releases it slowly.
Wood-fired ovens often reach temperatures upwards of 800°F (427°C).
Chef Mario Bellucci of Naples, Italy conducted a series of workshops across the United States starting September 1, 2023, renewing interest in wood-fired baking.
Bellucci has been a proponent of the wood-fired method since the early 2020s and believes modern appliances cannot fully replicate it.
Intense heat causes rapid gas expansion in dough, producing airy pockets in bread and 'oven spring' in pizza crusts.
Patricia Evans, a food scientist based in San Francisco, says the high heat accelerates Maillard reactions and caramelization, giving complex flavor.
Hardwoods like oak, maple, and birch are preferred because their density and low sap content let them burn hotter and longer with less smoke.
Jessica Thompson, CEO of Hearthwoods Sustainable Logging, insists on sustainably sourced hardwoods.
On November 12, 2023, baker Lucas Wright demonstrated flame management at the Regional Baking Summit in Denver.
Martha Goldstein, owner of the Rustic Loaf Bakery, said on October 5, 2023 that dough is 'a living thing' adjusted to its environment.
Wood-fired doughs are often higher in hydration and use longer fermentation times to withstand intense heat and develop flavor.
Bellucci hosted a weeklong event starting September 30, 2023, producing pizzas, roasted fish, smoked cheeses, and flaky pastries.
The 'Eco-Flame' oven was unveiled December 16, 2023 at the International Baking Expo, promising up to 50% less wood consumption via an air-recirculation system.
